arxiv-2108-11853.title: Lower bounds for integration and recovery in L 2 L_{2}
arxiv-2108-11853.creator: Aicke Hinrichs, David Krieg, Erich Novak, Jan Vybíral
arxiv-2108-11853.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aicke Hinrichs, David Krieg, Erich Novak, Jan Vybíral. Function values are, in some sense, “almost as good” as general linear information for L 2 L_{2} -approximation (optimal recovery, data assimilation) of functions from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This was recently proved by new upper bounds on the sampling numbers under the assumption that the singular values of the embedding of this Hilbert space into L 2 L_{2} are square-summable. Here we mainly prove new lower bounds .

arxiv-2401-00648.title: An example for Kuznetsov-Shinder conjecture
arxiv-2401-00648.creator: Tanya Kaushal Srivastava
arxiv-2401-00648.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tanya Kaushal Srivastava. We give an example for the Kuznetsov-Shinder conjecture, with infinitely many non-isomorphic but L-equivalent varieties. The Grothendieck ring of varieties Let k be a field of characteristic zero. One define the Grothendieck ring of varieties over k as the ring generated by isomorphism classes [X] of algebraic varieties X over k with relations [X]=[Z]+[U] for every closed subvariety Z\subset X having open complement U\subset X . The product structure of this ring is induced by the products of varieties.

arxiv-2511-14575.title: The Eddington Ratio Distribution of Narrow Line Active Galactic Nuclei
arxiv-2511-14575.creator: Michael R. Blanton, Arjun Suresh, Kyle B. Westfall, Dou Liu, John Moustakas
arxiv-2511-14575.description: Abstract We measure the Eddington ratio distribution of local optical narrow line active galactic nuclei (AGN) as a function of host galaxy properties. These measurements are a potential test of galaxy formation theories that predict supermassive black hole growth and feedback.

pmc-10753468.title: Treatment effectiveness of antibiotic therapy in Veterans with multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter spp. bacteremia
pmc-10753468.creator: Amanda Vivo, Margaret A. Fitzpatrick, Katie J. Suda, Geneva M. Wilson, Makoto M. Jones, Martin E. Evans, Charlesnika T. Evans
pmc-10753468.description: Objective:To describe antimicrobial therapy used for multidrug-resistant (MDR) Acinetobacter spp. bacteremia in Veterans and impacts on mortality.Methods:This was a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized Veterans Affairs patients from 2012 to 2018 with a positive MDR Acinetobacter spp. blood culture who received antimicrobial treatment 2 days prior to through 5 days after the culture date.

pmc-11506560.title: Hymecromone Promotes Longevity and Insulin Sensitivity in Mice
pmc-11506560.creator: Nadine Nagy, Kathryn S. Czepiel, Gernot Kaber, Darko Stefanovski, Aviv Hargil, Nina Pennetzdorfer, Robert Targ, Saranya C. Reghupaty, Thomas N. Wight, Robert B. Vernon, Rebecca L. Hull-Meichle, Payton Marshall, Carlos O. Medina, Hunter Martinez, Anissa Kalinowski, Rudolph D. Paladini, Stavros Garant
pmc-11506560.description: Given that the extracellular matrix polymer hyaluronan (HA) has been implicated in longevity, we asked whether 4-methylumbelliferone (4-MU), an inhibitor of HA synthesis, impacts lifespan in mice. We designed a prospective study of long-term administration of 4-MU with conventional C57BL/6J mice.

pmc-11616704.title: Dynamically logical modulation for THz wave within a dual gate–controlled 2DEG metasurface
pmc-11616704.creator: Hongxin Zeng, Xuan Cong, Huifang Zhang, Sen Gong, Tianchi Zhou, Lan Wang, Haoyi Cao, Huajie Liang, Shixiong Liang, Shiqi Wang, Feng Lan, Xun Wang, Ziqiang Yang, Yaxin Zhang, Tie Jun Cui
pmc-11616704.description: High-speed logic modulation of terahertz (THz) waves is crucial for future communications, yet a technology gap persists. Here, we report a dual gate–controlled two-dimensional electronic gas logic modulation metasurface that enables symmetric and asymmetric electron distribution states through independent control of the two electron transport channels.

pmc-12413184.title: How to Improve Pancreatic Cancer Network Care Using a Human-Centered Design Sprint
pmc-12413184.creator: Jana S Hopstaken, Mats Koeneman, Robin Hooijer, Concha C van Rijssel, Theo van Voorthuizen, Frank A Oort, Charlotte F J M Blanken, Martijn de Groot, Cees J H M van Laarhoven, Martijn W J Stommel, Naomi Cahill
pmc-12413184.description: Pancreatic cancer is considered a complex cancer requiring specific expertise in diagnostic workup and multimodality treatment. Often, multiple health care providers in different hospitals are involved during patient care. This fragmentation of care challenges health care providers in the network to deliver efficient, coherent, and continuous network care.

pmc-12478213.title: Affective Temperaments and Seasonality in Patients with Mood Disorders
pmc-12478213.creator: Matteo Di Vincenzo, Bianca Della Rocca, Gaia Sampogna, Claudia Toni, Arcangelo Di Cerbo, Stefano Calamaro, Florinda Guida, Anna Rita Atti, Silvia Tempia Valenta, Gabriele Sani, Mario Luciano, Andrea Fiorillo
pmc-12478213.description: BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) are complex and disabling mental disorders, requiring a clinical characterization to improve patients’ outcome. Affective temperaments and seasonality are associated with illness severity and prognosis in mood disorders, but are rarely explored in clinical practice.

pmc-13257495.title: Screening Impact of Anti-HDV Reflex Testing Among HBsAg-Positive Individuals
pmc-13257495.creator: Tor Regev-Sadeh, Ziv Neeman, Naama Schwartz, Orit Rozenberg, Fadi Abu Baker, Tarek Saadi, Mifleh Tatour, Rawi Hazzan
pmc-13257495.description: Background: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) causes one of the most severe forms of chronic viral hepatitis. Despite its severity, universal screening of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive individuals, as recommended by European guidelines, is not widely implemented. This study aimed to evaluate the yield of reflex HDV testing and to characterize HBV carriers who tested positive or negative for anti-HDV.

pmc-13282619.title: Maternal and child mental health and incident migraine in adolescence: An “All Our Families” prospective cohort study
pmc-13282619.creator: Kirsten Sjonnesen, Melanie Noel, Tamara Pringsheim, Scott B. Patten, Sheri Madigan, Prachi Khanna, Sheila McDonald, Paul E. Ronksley, Suzanne Tough, Serena L. Orr
pmc-13282619.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo examine the association between mental health symptoms in youth and their mothers, and youth incident migraine, using prospectively collected, longitudinal data from the “All Our Families” (AOF) cohort study.BackgroundInternalizing mental health symptoms, such as anxiety and depression, whether experienced by a child or his/her parent(s), have been linked to migraine and chronic pain conditions, but causal inferences have been limited by gaps in the current literature.
